cards.title: Plan
cards.description: Hierophant: plan for a merge-ready change, not a draft
cards.prompt:
Create an implementation plan for the current task. Do not write code. No filler.

From context, note (do not over-ask):
- acceptance criteria (what counts as done);
- scope: IN / OUT;
- risks: data, API, races, compatibility, regressions.

Requirements:
1. Small verifiable steps; each has a deliverable + how to verify.
2. Account for tests, errors, edge cases, rollback.
3. Simple working solution beats "ideal" architecture.
4. Explicit: assumptions and open questions.
5. Plan only.

Output: numbered plan + short risk list + definition of done.

cards.title: Review
cards.description: Justice: review with project quality score 0–10
cards.prompt:
Strict review of the current plan or diff/result.

Set project quality score 0–10:
- 0–6 — block: cannot continue / merge;
- 7–8 — acceptable with caveats;
- 9–10 — high bar.
Below 7 = blocker. For normal review, ≥ 7 is enough; 10 is not required.

Check:
1. Correctness and edge cases
2. Regressions and fragility
3. Readability, cohesion, unnecessary complexity
4. Tests and error handling
5. Security and data (if relevant)
6. Top 3 fixes for the next PR

Format:
- Project quality score: N/10
- Verdict: block (<7) / acceptable (7–8) / strong (9–10)
- Findings: Critical / Major / Minor
- Specific fixes (files/places if known)

Large refactoring only on request. Do not accept "good enough" below 7.

cards.title: Refine
cards.description: Temperance: trim the plan to the minimum needed for implementation
cards.prompt:
Improve the current plan or design to implementation-ready level.

Rules:
1. Cut everything outside acceptance criteria.
2. Clarify vague parts: interfaces, data, errors, tests.
3. If bloated — propose simpler with trade-offs.
4. Keep steps and verification method.
5. No code until asked.

Output: full updated plan + changelog (3–7 items) + expected plan readiness score 0–10.

cards.title: Code
cards.description: Magician: next step — verifiable code without regressions
cards.prompt:
Implement the next open step of the approved plan.

Rules:
1. Only this step — no "while we're at it".
2. No regressions: preserve existing behavior.
3. Handle errors explicitly; do not swallow exceptions.
4. Missing data — 1–3 precise questions, do not invent APIs.
5. After: what changed · how to verify · risks.

Status: done / partial / blocked + why.
Step goal — confident project quality score ≥ 7/10 on correctness.

cards.title: Test
cards.description: Star: prove with a green run, not a promise
cards.prompt:
Verify what was just done as in CI, not "should work".

Do:
1. Commands/tests/build; show actual output.
2. Happy path + at least one failure/edge (or why not possible).
3. Red — root cause + minimal fix or blocker.
4. Green — "TEST PASSED" + list of checks.
5. On red, do not move to the next step.

Result: green/red + preliminary project quality score 0–10 (below 7 = not ready).

cards.title: Fix
cards.description: Tower: minimal patch until quality score ≥ 7
cards.prompt:
Fix the defect from the last test, review, or project quality score < 7.

Rules:
1. Minimal fix — no "while we're at it" refactoring.
2. Symptom → cause → blast radius.
3. Patch → verify the same way the bug was caught.
4. before → after → evidence.
5. Repeat until score / test is ≥ 7.
6. Blocker — 2 options with trade-offs.

New features forbidden while the defect is open.

cards.title: Polish
cards.description: Strength: raise project quality score to 9–10
cards.prompt:
High-quality polish mode. Stopping at 7–8 is forbidden. Goal — project quality score 9 or 10 out of 10.

Project quality score scale:
- <7 — fail;
- 7–8 — "merge under pressure", not enough for this card;
- 9–10 — stop.

Loop without "continue?":
1. Project quality score N/10 + findings holding the score (Critical/Major).
2. If ≤ 8 — fixes only for those (scope freeze, no new features).
3. Re-run checks.
4. New project quality score.
5. While ≤ 8 — repeat.

Stop only at 9 or 10. Report:
- Project quality score: N/10
- What raised quality
- Residual risk (if any)
- What you did not touch and why

If ceiling is below 9 due to external constraints — name them and max achievable score, but first exhaust fixes within scope.

cards.title: Cycle
cards.description: World: end-to-end, each item ≥ 7 quality points
cards.prompt:
Full end-to-end cycle through the plan.

An item is closed only at project quality score ≥ 7. Use "Polish" for 9–10.

For each item:
1. Name the item.
2. Implement.
3. Verify with facts (commands/tests/scenario).
4. Project quality score 0–10.
5. If < 7 — fix until ≥ 7.
6. Next item.

Forbidden: skipping steps, inflating scope, masking red tests.
No plan — first a short plan (5–8 steps) with acceptance criteria, then execution.

Final:
- overall project quality score 0–10;
- done / not done;
- residual risks;
- what to verify manually before merge.
